summary_md: Paul's own research plan (dated 2026-09-25) for testing whether industries spend more or less on federal politics when they have grown, are growing, or expect to grow. It specifies OLS with a separate intercept per sector, six core tests (C1-C3 contributions, L1-L3 lobbying, each with prior actual, same-year actual, or IBISWorld predicted growth), election-cycle dummies and IEM expected-control covariates, plus job-tier and per-chamber Democratic-share extensions. Its strongest contributions are discipline rules: predicted growth must come from a report vintage published before the spending year, missing forecasts stay missing, null results are kept, and independent-row OLS errors are ruled insufficient with nine or fewer sector clusters. It reports no estimates, and its own readiness check says contributions overlap the IEM forecasts only in 2021-2022. The document is the north star of the built sector growth study (Mentat sector_growth_study, in R). The build honours the inference caution with a wild cluster restricted bootstrap by sector and Holm adjustment, but departs from the plan in three places: log outcomes rather than dollar levels, a retrospective 2023-2026 expected-control series plus 538 robustness filling the IEM gap, and added Tossup and trend terms. Results recorded in the brain (UNVERIFIED, single path): L3 on LobbyView lobbying b 0.242 million 2025 USD per pp (p 0.033, Holm 0.1125) flips to -0.477 under year FE, growth adds no adjusted R2, and the annual partisan SHIFT is -0.04 (p 0.76). So far the plan's question is answered as no stable growth signal, which bears directly on the live giving forecast that still feeds IBISWorld growth into general giving at 50/50.

bearings.paper_claim: Six core tests C1-C3 and L1-L3: Y_it = a_i + b X_it + Pres + Midterm + ExpectedDemHouse + ExpectedDemSenate (+ current control for lobbying), Y in millions of 2025 USD, X one growth measure at a time in pp; keep all six results including nulls; nine planned sectors give few clusters so independent-row OLS errors are not sufficient.
bearings.system_side: The built study implements the plan in R with sector baselines, one growth regressor per test, and a wild cluster restricted bootstrap-t by sector with Webb six-point weights (all 6^G vectors when feasible) plus Holm over L1-L3; it departs by modelling log giving with Tossup and Trend terms rather than dollar levels.
bearings.transfer_conditions: Direct: the plan is the declared north star of this lane. The level-vs-log departure changes coefficient units (effect on log dollars vs millions) and should be labelled amended, not original, under the brain's contract-row rule.

bearings.paper_claim: Readiness check: verified contribution years overlap IEM congressional forecasts only in 2021-2022; IEM covers 2008-2022 with 2023-2025 missing, and the later election result must never substitute for a missing forecast.
bearings.system_side: The build fills 2023-2026 from a separate expected_control_2023_2026 series with method and flag carried, adds the 538 generic ballot as robustness family H4-538, and flags values measured after the spending year (exp_dem_*_after_year); the component record calls 2023/2025 expectations retrospective.
bearings.transfer_conditions: Holds only if the 2023-2026 series is a dated pre-election expectation; if it was built with knowledge of outcomes it breaks the plan's own timing rule and H4 exp_dem estimates must carry that label.

bearings.paper_claim: Do not add full year indicators while keeping national annual controls (year effects absorb them); a separate check may swap the controls for year indicators to see whether the growth relationship survives common yearly shocks.
bearings.paper_location: Section 3, paragraph after the control table
bearings.system_side: The build runs the year-FE variant as that separate check; the recorded result is that L3-LV b +0.352 flips to -0.477 with sector and year FE, log-FE -0.006, and growth adds no adjusted R2 (0.884717 vs 0.884690). The check the plan prescribed is what defeated the headline estimate.
bearings.transfer_conditions: Results come from a single analysis path and stay UNVERIFIED until a second path reproduces them (DE-062); a pooled slope is UNSTRATIFIED unless the SLOPES per-sector strata are quoted alongside.

bearings.paper_claim: Predicted industry growth (C3) is the variable of direct interest; the sign of the growth-spending relation is to be estimated, not assumed, and IBISWorld forecasts proxy public expectations only.
bearings.system_side: The live giving forecast multiplies the anchor by (1 + x/2), where x is the industry budget change implied by the IBISWorld real growth path with a one-year lag (the 50/50); company PACs were moved off it (D-116), but general giving still carries it.
bearings.transfer_conditions: The plan's own study has so far found no stable growth effect (sign flips under year FE; no adjusted R2 gain), so the 50/50 growth term rests on an owner ruling rather than on this plan's evidence; transfer also assumes the study population (company rosters) matches the forecast measures, which Paul ruled a stated limitation.

bearings.paper_claim: Partisan direction is tested with a per-chamber Democratic share D/(D+R), zero denominators missing, using the matching chamber's expected and current control; party and presidential committee flows are not assigned to a chamber.
bearings.system_side: The build's annual SHIFT test (RShare on Shift = P - RMajNow) found no stable shift (-0.04, p 0.76); the weekly SEATS-W extension, which the plan does not specify, found -3.47 pp D share per expected D seat in the 2022 House using dated 538 forecasts.
bearings.transfer_conditions: SEATS-W is one election and goes beyond the plan's annual design; the plan supplies only the outcome definition.

gaps_exposed: The plan prescribes dollar-level outcomes; the build models log giving, so reported coefficients are not in the plan's millions-of-2025-USD units and the original-vs-amended label needs to be explicit per contract row.

Contribution history before 2021 is not established locally (plan Section 6B; the brain records no pre-2021 cycle beyond the 2020 extension), so C1-C3 rest on very few years per sector and the full control specification stays weakly identified.

The live giving forecast keeps an IBISWorld growth term at 50/50 for general giving although the growth study found no stable growth effect; no recorded backtest shows whether that term beats the cycle-only model.
Credit Arms, P and C, Telecom, life insurance and auto lack LDA sector totals; the four-sector LDA aggregate does not cover the nine-sector design, so L1-L3 run on LobbyView with fewer clusters.
The Chief tier uses a non-date-specific executive-name override and the Employee tier absorbs unrecognized titles; no dated-role sensitivity test is recorded in the build.
With G sectors the wild cluster bootstrap cannot reach p below 2/6^G; tests with few sectors return no inference by design, which the plan anticipated but did not size.
flags: Possible conflict with the plan's own rule: 2023-2026 expected control in the build is described as retrospective, while the plan says the later election result must never substitute for a missing forecast; verify the series is dated pre-election before quoting H4 exp_dem results.
Recorded growth-study results (L3-LV 0.242, Holm 0.1125; year-FE flip to -0.477; SHIFT -0.04) come from a single analysis path and stay UNVERIFIED under DE-062.
Any pooled common growth slope across the nine sectors must be quoted with the SLOPES strata or labelled UNSTRATIFIED.
LDA expenditure is used here as a spending outcome, not as an SNA edge or weight, so D-021 is not breached; LDA totals from this lane should not flow into network weights.
No paul_entries and no annotations exist; the document itself is Paul's, so alignment is judged against the brain record.
paul_alignment: Agrees: the plan says estimate the sign, keep nulls and distrust small-cluster OLS errors; the build did so and found no stable growth effect and no stable annual partisan shift. Partly stale: it names statsmodels and IEM only, while the study runs in R with log outcomes, 538 robustness, a 2023-2026 expected-control series and a 2020 extension; the 2021-2022 overlap warning is only partly resolved. The live 50/50 IBISWorld growth term in general giving (ruled 2026-10-07) is not supported by this plan's results.

related.why: The plan's sector-FE design and its year-FE check are the two-way FE setting Imai and Kim caution about; Paul highlighted it for this lane.
Firm lobbying returns motivate the deep-pockets versus seek-relief hypotheses that the plan leaves sign-agnostic.
Links corporate lobbying and PAC spending to market concentration, an alternative industry-condition driver to revenue growth.
Lobbying ROI evidence underlies the idea that weak forecasts could prompt lobbying for favourable policy.
Low overlap between lobbying and PAC spenders supports the plan's rule to keep contributions and lobbying as separate outcomes.
Sequential donation-lobbying links bear on the plan's separate C and L models and on lead-lag between them.
Election-cycle synchronization of lobbying supports the plan's Pres and Midterm controls in the lobbying equations.
The cross-industry political spending memo draws on the same sector spending sources and rosters.
Paul's cross-industry finance and LDA report uses the same Mentat and LDA sector spending data the plan joins.
